meta.name: LevelBridge starter data
meta.subject: Maths (Class 1-10 continuous ladder)
meta.note: Starter content written with AI help. A teacher must review it against the school's own textbook before classroom use.

levels.name: Numbers to 99 and counting

teacherActivity.title: Number bead line-up
steps: Lay number flashcards 1 to 99 on the floor in sequence.
Call out a number ('find forty-seven') and ask students to point.
Ask what comes immediately before and after the target number.

levels.selfPractice: Complete missing number sequences in blocks of ten (e.g. 31, 32, __, 34).

levels.name: Two-digit addition and subtraction, tables 2/5/10

teacherActivity.title: Tens and units with sticks
steps: Show numbers as bundles of ten sticks and loose single sticks.
To subtract with regrouping, unbundle one ten into ten ones.
Practice skip counting rhythmically by 2, 5, and 10.

levels.selfPractice: Pair practice: one partner creates a two-digit sum with counters, the other writes and solves.

levels.name: Multiplication tables to 10, 3-digit place value

teacherActivity.title: Array grids and place value houses
steps: Draw arrays of dots (e.g., 4 rows of 6) to connect repeated addition to multiplication.
Use three columns (Hundreds, Tens, Ones) with digit cards.
Chant multiplication tables 3 through 9 with clapping rhythms.

levels.selfPractice: Fill in blank cells on a 10 × 10 multiplication grid with a partner.

levels.name: Division, 4-digit numbers

teacherActivity.title: Fair sharing and thousand blocks
steps: Distribute 24 counters equally into 4 cups to model 24 ÷ 4 = 6.
Introduce remainders using 25 counters divided into 4 cups.
Build 4-digit numbers using thousands, hundreds, tens, and units cards.

levels.selfPractice: Solve short division puzzle cards and check answers using multiplication.

levels.name: Fractions and decimals

teacherActivity.title: Paper strip folding
steps: Fold paper strips into halves, fourths, and eighths to show equivalent fractions.
Shade 3 out of 10 parts on a grid to represent both 3/10 and 0.3.
Add simple like fractions together on a number line.

levels.selfPractice: Match fraction cards (like 1/2, 2/4, 0.5) to their visual shaded diagrams.

levels.name: Factors, multiples, ratio, integers

teacherActivity.title: Factor trees and temperature lines
steps: Build factor rainbows for 24 and 36 on the chalkboard.
Draw a vertical thermometer line showing positive and negative integers.
Model simple ratios using red and blue bottle caps.

levels.selfPractice: Work in pairs to list all factors of given numbers and find their HCF.

levels.name: Percentages, simple equations

teacherActivity.title: Hundred square grid and balance scales
steps: Use 10x10 grids to convert fractions to percentages (e.g., 1/4 = 25%).
Draw a balance scale showing 'x + 5 = 12' to illustrate inverse operations.
Have students subtract 5 from both pans to isolate x.

levels.selfPractice: Solve one-step equation cards and substitute answers back to check balance.

levels.name: Algebraic expressions, linear equations, squares and roots

teacherActivity.title: Algebra tiles and square grids
steps: Group like terms using colored algebra tiles (x-tiles vs unit squares).
Solve two-step linear equations: subtract constant, then divide by coefficient.
Illustrate squares and square roots using physical square dot arrays.

levels.selfPractice: Simplify algebraic expressions by combining like terms on practice cards.

levels.name: Linear equations and graphs

teacherActivity.title: Coordinate plane plotting
steps: Draw Cartesian axes on grid board; plot (x, y) coordinates.
Graph lines like y = 2x + 1 by making an input-output table.
Demonstrate gradient / slope as vertical rise over horizontal run.

levels.selfPractice: Plot coordinate pairs on grid paper and determine the slope of the line.

levels.name: Quadratic equations (factorising) and Pythagoras

teacherActivity.title: Factor cross-method and 3-4-5 triangle
steps: Factorise x^2 + 7x + 12 by finding two numbers that multiply to 12 and add to 7.
Verify roots by substituting x = -3 and x = -4.
Construct a 3-4-5 right triangle and verify a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

levels.selfPractice: Factorise quadratic expressions and solve for hypotenuses of right triangles.

digits_reversed.label: Digits swapped
digits_reversed.explanation: Look at place values: tens and ones are different columns. 54 is 5 tens and 4 ones, not 45.

expanded_form_written_together.label: Wrote expanded form as digits
expanded_form_written_together.explanation: When you write fifty-four, 50 and 4 combine into 54 without extra zeros.

count_offset.label: Count shifted
count_offset.explanation: Count one by one carefully to avoid being one ahead or behind.

add_instead_of_subtract.label: Added instead of subtracting
add_instead_of_subtract.explanation: Check the sign: minus (-) means take away, while plus (+) means combine.

subtracted_smaller_from_larger_digit.label: Subtracted smaller digit from larger without regrouping
subtracted_smaller_from_larger_digit.explanation: When subtracting ones, if the bottom digit is bigger, borrow 1 ten from the tens column first.

borrowing_tens_not_reduced.label: Forgot to reduce tens after borrowing
borrowing_tens_not_reduced.explanation: Remember: when you borrow 1 ten, reduce the tens digit by 1 before finishing.

table_skip_error.label: Multiplication skip-count off by one step
table_skip_error.explanation: Count groups carefully: 6 × 7 means 6 groups of 7, which is 42.

added_instead_of_multiplied.label: Added instead of multiplying
added_instead_of_multiplied.explanation: Multiplication means repeated groups, not simply adding the two numbers.

place_value_shift.label: Place value column confused
place_value_shift.explanation: Check hundreds, tens, and units columns to keep each digit in its correct value.

remainder_ignored.label: Remainder overlooked
remainder_ignored.explanation: When dividing, any leftover amount must be accounted for as a remainder or fraction.

division_by_wrong_step.label: Division step miscalculated
division_by_wrong_step.explanation: Think: what number multiplied by the divisor gives the dividend?

added_numerators_and_denominators.label: Added denominators together
added_numerators_and_denominators.explanation: When adding fractions with common denominators, add only the numerators: 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5.

multiplied_instead_of_divided_fraction.label: Fraction operation reversed
multiplied_instead_of_divided_fraction.explanation: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal (flip the second fraction).

decimal_place_shift.label: Decimal point misaligned
decimal_place_shift.explanation: Align decimal points vertically before adding or subtracting decimals.

percent_as_decimal_shift.label: Percentage conversion shifted
percent_as_decimal_shift.explanation: Percent means per hundred: 70% is 70/100 = 0.7, not 0.07 or 7.0.

ratio_order_swapped.label: Ratio order reversed
ratio_order_swapped.explanation: Keep terms in the order given: ratio of red to blue means red comes first.

sign_error.label: Negative sign rule error
sign_error.explanation: Subtracting a negative number is equivalent to adding: 5 - (-3) = 5 + 3 = 8.

only_one_side.label: Applied operation to only one side of equation
only_one_side.explanation: An equation is a balance: whatever you do to the left side, do to the right side.

combined_unlike_terms.label: Combined unlike algebraic terms
combined_unlike_terms.explanation: You can only combine like terms (e.g., 3x and 2x combine to 5x, but 3x + 2 remains 3x + 2).

slope_formula_inverted.label: Inverted gradient / slope
slope_formula_inverted.explanation: Gradient is rise over run: (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1), vertical change over horizontal change.

quadratic_sign_error.label: Signs swapped in factorisation
quadratic_sign_error.explanation: Check your factors by expanding back: (x + a)(x + b) must give the middle term and constant.

pythagoras_added_not_squared.label: Added legs without squaring
pythagoras_added_not_squared.explanation: Pythagoras theorem states a^2 + b^2 = c^2, so square both legs before adding.

area_perimeter_confusion.label: Confused area with perimeter
area_perimeter_confusion.explanation: Area is space inside (length × width), while perimeter is distance around the outside.

questions.prompt: In the number 472, what is the value of the digit 7?
In 5,420, what is the value of the digit 5?
What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 12 and 18?
In a class of 12 boys and 8 girls, what is the ratio of boys to girls in simplest form?
What is 70% written as a decimal?
A price increased from 50 to 60. What is the percentage increase?
If x = 4, what is the value of 2x + 3?
What is the slope (gradient) of the line passing through (2, 2) and (5, 8)?
What is the y-intercept of the line y = 3x - 5?
If 2x + 3y = 12 and x = 3, what is y?
A right-angled triangle has legs of lengths 3 cm and 4 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
In a right triangle, hypotenuse is 10 cm and one leg is 6 cm. What is the other leg?
What are the roots of the equation (x - 4)(x + 1) = 0?
